evidence: Skill reference quality-checks.md:9-11 says to read instruction.md cold; defect = numbered acceptance lists, a shall/must spec table, a feature matrix, or a build recipe (framework, file layout, endpoint list). task/instruction.md is 5 lines / 116 words, three first-person prose paragraphs: instruction.md:1 "I'd like a small local playground for working on JavaScript and complete HTML files. The editor itself matters: I often paste a long one-line experiment, format it, make changes in several places, and then run it beside the source."; instruction.md:3 points to the six notes in /instructions and /assets/seed_data.json; instruction.md:5 "Put the app in /app and serve the workspace at /. I should be able to open it, edit code, run it and inspect the result without signing in." It gives a motive and a usage story, and contains no numbered or bulleted list, no table, no shall/MUST wording, no framework, file layout or endpoint list (a regex scan for list markers, table pipes and shall/MUST across instruction.md and all six notes returned nothing). The only path facts in the brief are /app, / and the two input locations, which check 4 requires. The six notes (1803 words) are dense, especially ui.md (817 words) and behaviour.md (491 words), but they are headed prose paragraphs in the same first-person voice (overview.md:3 "while I work", behaviour.md:11 "must not touch what I'm doing"), not acceptance checklists; integration.md:3-9 states start command, port, health path and SQLite/DB_PATH, which is the runtime contract the template profile mandates rather than a task-added build recipe, and integration.md:5 / policy.md:3 leave routes, frontend tools, layout, labels and schema to the builder. Counterexample attempts: (a) a spec-sheet reading - ui.md enumerates many editor behaviours with 'must' in lower case several times (ui.md:5, ui.md:7), which is the closest the task comes to a spec; it stays descriptive prose about what the user does and the check as written targets instruction.md, so this does not reach the defect bar; (b) a build-recipe reading - ui.md:3 bans textarea/contenteditable and named editor libraries, but that is the product's defining constraint (a self-built editor), not a prescribed stack. Template instruction.md is only the CHANGE_ME placeholder, so there is no template-controlled wording to preserve or violate.
